original_question: Let M be a separable subfactor with two embeddings pi_i: M -> NU. Suppose phi_n: N -> N is a sequence of unital completely positive maps whose ultrapower Phi = (phi_n)^U conjugates pi1 to pi2. Determine whether there must exist a unitary u in NU that conjugates pi1 and pi2.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it has a separable subfactor M, two embeddings pi_1, pi_2 into N^U, a sequence of unital completely positive maps phi_n : N -> N inducing an ultrapower map, and it asks whether this u.c.p.-level conjugacy forces unitary conjugacy inside N^U. That is exactly the content-pattern of Problem 31. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The paper fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ in its opening notation, so the question should state that U is fixed and that N^U denotes the tracial ultrapower.
The ambient setting is tracial von Neumann algebras / II_1-factor ultrapowers; that context should be stated explicitly rather than left implicit.
It should specify that pi_1 and pi_2 are embeddings M -> N^U in the operator-algebraic sense (normally understood as unital *-embeddings).
The induced map Phi = (phi_n)^U should be identified as a map N^U -> N^U.
The phrase "Phi conjugates pi_1 to pi_2" should be made explicit as the intertwining relation Phi o pi_1 = pi_2.
The conclusion should spell out unitary conjugacy pointwise: there exists a unitary u in N^U such that u pi_1(x) u^* = pi_2(x) for all x in M.
To stay maximally faithful to the paper's wording, one should preserve the term "subfactor" and avoid silently replacing the setting by a broader abstract category.

No extra assumptions such as amenability, Connes embeddability, trace preservation of the phi_n, or automorphic conjugacy appear in Problem 31, so the refined question should neither add nor substitute them.
refined_question: Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, and let N^U denote the tracial ultrapower of the ambient II_1 factor N. Let M be a separable subfactor, and let pi_1, pi_2 : M -> N^U be embeddings. Suppose there exists a sequence of unital completely positive maps phi_n : N -> N such that the induced ultrapower map Phi = (phi_n)^U : N^U -> N^U satisfies Phi o pi_1 = pi_2. Must there exist a unitary u in N^U such that u pi_1(x) u^* = pi_2(x) for every x in M?
justification: This paper is not organized around a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 relevant to your draft; instead, your draft matches Problem 31 in the section "Lifting problems" almost verbatim. The paper's opening notation paragraph supplies the fixed ultrafilter U and the notation N^U for tracial ultrapowers, while the nearby discussion after Problem 33 places this block among Jung-type conjugacy questions. So the right refinement is to make the ultrapower notation and the meanings of "conjugates" and "unitarily conjugates" explicit, without broadening the question beyond Problem 31 itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
